findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded logs
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver, so the returned logger writes its `InfoLogs`/`DebugLogs`/... counters into a throwaway instance. Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now always goes through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)`, any test that injects `plog.NewTestLogger()` into the middleware and then asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will observe zero calls — either failing outright or, worse, silently passing assertions that expect nothing to be logged. The fake should return `f` (optionally recording the ctx) so logging through the contextual path remains observable.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests and the moved log fields are unverified
findings.body: This PR moves the `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` fields out of the explicit log params in `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` and into context attributes set by the brand-new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, but no test is added for the new middleware and no test asserts that the "Plugin Request Completed" log line still carries those fields. The correctness now depends on (a) the middleware being registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain and (b) `log.WithContextualAttributes` attributes being picked up by `Logger.FromContext`. A silent regression here would drop fields that log-based dashboards/alerts rely on, with nothing in CI to catch it.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported plugins/log.Logger interface is a breaking change
findings.body: `plugins/log.Logger` is an exported interface consumed across the plugin packages and by out-of-tree code (e.g. grafana-enterprise). Adding the `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method breaks every existing implementation that is not updated in this PR; only the two in-tree implementations (`grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger`) were adjusted, and the `var _ Logger = ...` compile checks only cover those. Any external or generated implementation will fail to compile after this change, so it needs to be coordinated/announced or the method should be introduced via an optional extension interface.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops contextual fields if the concrete type assertion fails
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` asserts the result of `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and, on failure, falls back to `d.New()` — a logger with no context attributes at all. The failure path is silent: if `infra/log` ever returns a different `Logger` implementation from `FromContext`, every plugin request log line would silently lose `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` and `traceID`, with no error or warning to indicate why. Consider storing the `log.Logger` interface in the wrapper instead of the concrete `*ConcreteLogger`, so no assertion is needed.

findings.title: Logger name still "plugin.instrumentation" after the rename
findings.body: `NewLoggerMiddleware` is still constructed with `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")`, so the emitted log lines carry `logger=plugin.instrumentation` even though the instrumentation middleware has been renamed to the metrics middleware and the contextual logging has been split out. Since the goal of this change is naming consistency, and this name is user-visible in logs (and used for per-logger level configuration), it should be updated to something that matches the new structure (e.g. `plugin.logger`/`plugin.request`), keeping in mind that changing it affects existing log filters.
